$comment: The frontend coverage policy. Hand-curated; the measured numbers live in
coverage-baseline.json, which is machine-written. Rationale and the local
$comment:domains: Behavioural logic only. `components/` is deliberately absent apart from
`components/providers/`: a rendered row is presentational boilerplate and
covering it inflates the percentage without buying confidence, which is the
failure mode issue #700 asks to avoid. Membership is by GLOB, so a new store
or service is inside the gate the moment it is written rather than whenever
somebody remembers to add it to a list.

domains.why: Zustand stores hold the client's own truth — engagement, identity, scroll position, invalidation signals.
Every network call the app makes and the shapes it expects back.
Session, query client, query keys, share intents, telemetry, platform forks.
The on-device feed cache, its schema and its migrations.
Boot order, auth routing and account-switch teardown — the components that are logic.
Where the app's product behaviour actually lives.
Pure logic: intent parsing, post building, feed merging, formatting.

$comment:criticalPathBar: The seven areas issue #700 names, held materially higher than anything a
global percentage asks for. Branches matter more than statements here: a
permission check, a consent gate and a cursor boundary are all branches, and
a test that walks the happy path covers every statement in them.
$comment:belowBarExemptions: Critical-path files that do NOT clear the bar today. This list is the honest
half of the policy: it says out loud which named-critical code is untested,
rather than lowering the bar until everything passes. Each entry still
carries its measured pin in coverage-baseline.json, so an exempt file cannot
get worse — only stay put or improve. `expectedCounts.belowBarExemptions` is
an equality, so the list cannot grow quietly, and an entry that starts
clearing the bar is reported as a failure until it is deleted.

components/providers/AuthRouter.tsx.reason: AuthRouter.test.tsx covers the routing decisions but not the cold-boot restore branches, which need the 5-25s SSO window a jest run cannot reproduce.

hooks/usePostLike.ts.reason: No direct test. usePostSave.ts is the covered sibling and the shape to copy; the optimistic-write and rollback paths are the ones that matter.

hooks/usePostBoost.ts.reason: No direct test. Boosts write through postsStore and must reach engagementInvalidation; neither leg is asserted anywhere today.

hooks/usePostVote.ts.reason: No direct test. It is one of the two call sites that write invalidation through the store rather than the hooks, so a regression here is invisible to the hook-level tests.

hooks/usePostActions.tsx.reason: No direct test. Mostly menu assembly, but it is where the operated-account and channel refusals are applied.

stores/postsStore.ts.reason: postsStoreGranularReactivity.test.tsx covers selector reactivity only. The engagement write path — the authority every post surface reads — is largely unasserted.

utils/postBuilder.ts.reason: Covered indirectly through compose tests. The quote, poll and scheduled variants each add branches nothing exercises directly.

services/channelDeletionService.ts.reason: No direct test. Its siblings channelAccountService and channelWritersService are both at 100%; this one is the destructive operation and is the odd one out.

hooks/useExternalActorResolve.ts.reason: No direct test. externalActorQuery.test.ts covers the query shape, not the hook's federated-handle branches.

hooks/useMentionNode.ts.reason: No direct test. Self-hosted node pairing state; low traffic, but it is federation-facing state as the issue defines it.

hooks/useFediversePreferredLanguage.ts.reason: No direct test. Reads and writes a consent-adjacent Oxy setting.

lib/shareIntent.ts.reason: The neutral default of a platform split; the native fork is where the work happens. Kept on the critical list because a deep link landing in the wrong composer is a data-loss bug.

lib/shareIntent.native.ts.reason: No direct test. expo-share-intent's module surface needs a mock nobody has written; utils/composeIntent.ts, at 97%, is the parser it feeds.

hooks/useFeedState.ts.reason: Two test files cover memory mode and the auth-identity keying. Pagination, the pending/refetch path and scroll restoration are the uncovered remainder.

stores/feedScrollStore.ts.reason: feedScrollStore.test.ts covers retention and keying; the eviction and warm-start branches are not asserted.

db/cacheLifecycle.ts.reason: Clears the statement bar, not the branch bar. The uncovered branches are the SQLite-unavailable fallbacks, which only run on web where isDbAvailable() is false.

$comment:unenforceable: jest-expo resolves the NATIVE platform extension, so `import './X'` never
loads `X.web.tsx`. Measured on this repository: a syntax error inserted into
Feed.web.tsx left the whole suite green. A test that names `../X.web`
explicitly DOES load it — which is why three web forks here carry real
coverage and are pinned like anything else. These three are reachable by no
implicit path and have no direct test, so a coverage floor on them would be
a number nobody can move. tsc and `expo export --platform web` are their
gates. The policy fails if one of them gains coverage and stays on this list.

lib/chunkReload.web.ts.reason: Web-only fork, no direct test; jest resolves lib/chunkReload.native.ts instead.

lib/hlsPlayback.web.ts.reason: Web-only fork, no direct test; jest resolves lib/hlsPlayback.native.ts instead.

lib/socketBfcache.web.ts.reason: Web-only fork, no direct test; jest resolves lib/socketBfcache.native.ts instead.

$comment:jestOwnedThresholds: Pre-existing hard floors in package.json's jest config. They stay there — the
policy asserts the numbers rather than re-implementing them, so that lowering
one is a failure here as well as a lie there. viewerQueryKeys.ts at 100% is
the boundary that keeps one account's cached data out of another's.
$comment:allowedBaselineDecreases: Dated, path-and-metric-named permission to record a LOWER baseline than the
base revision — the one legitimate case being code that legitimately shrank.
An entry that is not currently excusing a real decrease fails, so this list
cannot become a standing permission slip.
$comment:expectedCounts: Equalities, not bounds. Each of these lists is a way to switch the gate off
one defensible line at a time, and a bound cannot tell growth from shrinkage.
